headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx reads Claude Code post-tool events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, while haystack can use MCP servers. That creates a plausible bridge for attacker-controlled content to flow from one agent into the other as instructions. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ctx observes content produced by haystack through MCP or files without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF haystack forwards retrieved text into ctx-managed workflows, ctx may treat it as trusted context.
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text.
Restrict MCP channels to allowlisted schemas.
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers; haystack has broad network egress and can use MCP servers. Even though haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, the pair can still move local data into outbound requests or logs in default workflows. The shared MCP/file path makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF ctx stores sensitive workspace content in files or logs, haystack can transmit it via outbound requests.
IF both agents connect to the same MCP server, data may cross trust boundaries.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Block outbound requests from sensitive directories.
Rotate or redact logs before sharing them.
Audit MCP server endpoints for data handling.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and filesystem access; haystack has broad network egress and MCP use. Overlap on shared mutable resources is plausible, but the profiles do not prove unrestricted concurrent writes to the same directory, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path, state races can occur.
IF both agents mutate the same MCP-backed resource, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent runs on shared state.
Check for stale artifacts before each run.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a harness/context manager and haystack is a search-RAG system, so haystack outputs can plausibly become ctx inputs without a verification step. That creates a default pathway where one agent’s generated or retrieved text is treated as authoritative by the other, but no downstream action authority is shown, so medium fits.
conditions: IF haystack outputs are consumed by ctx as trusted context, errors can cascade.
IF ctx forwards haystack results into later tool calls without verification, falsehoods propagate.
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse.
Insert a human review step for high-impact outputs.
Compare haystack answers against a second source.
Mark retrieved text as untrusted in prompts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data, while haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, so the only compliance concern is a documented-gap style overlap rather than a proven breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but the evidence is thin.
conditions: IF ctx logs regulated data into audit/runtime logs, retention policy review is required.
IF haystack is configured to store more than anonymous usage statistics, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Confirm data-class inventory before deployment.
Shorten log retention to the minimum needed.
Disable collection of unnecessary telemetry.
Review residency settings on connected services.
requires-engineering: document and enforce compliance boundaries.
